lists.label: Settings
lists.holds: One row per tool and scope (a person, a film, a piece or the whole account): the settings that tool reads when it runs, as JSON.

instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "Work out the nutrients in my recipe, per batch and per 100 g, against the daily intakes an adult needs", and give it datasets.
2. The AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:work-out-a-recipes-nutrients-from-fooddata-central and its input (the worked example shows one).

3. Read what comes back: Takes a recipe (each ingredient's FoodData Central food id and grams, or a count of a portion such as 2 tbsp) and the person's FoodData Central CSV downloads, and works out 33 nutrients for the whole batch and per 100 g of mix, each ingredient's share, and % of the adult 19-30 Dietary Reference Intake for men and women, with a flag: gap, low, meets a third or more, meets a full day, a limit (sodium), or unknown_lower_bound_only where a main ingredient has no value.
4. It reads and writes only its own rows through the records door: record:setting (records:read).

pour.how: Name the list you already keep for the same job and read it with records:read (its fields and row type). Run tool:pour-example-rows-into-my-list with that list as into and this kit list as kit_list: it matches each kit field to one of yours (your map, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), pours nothing under 80% and names the fields with no home, and otherwise answers the one records:write that adds the example rows beside your own.
